report_html:
A Balanced Attack

There's no bell-cow to bank on — the lead back sees just 40% of carries (league ~59%), a committee that caps any one back's ceiling and makes their rushing props matchup- and script-dependent.

The Offensive Blueprint

This is an aggressive, pass-leaning attack: +1% pass rate over expected, top of the league's range, and no interest in sitting on a lead (43% pass when ahead).

The tight end is barely used in the passing game (9% of targets vs ~15%) — fade their TE's receiving props.

Their backs are a real part of the passing game — RBs see 21% of targets (vs ~18%), which props up the back's reception floor.

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is pass-first (54% pass), which puts scoring equity on the WR1.

Defense — They Force the Throw

They surrender 102 rushing and 226 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). They wall the run and force the throw — attack with the opposing WR room.

A stingy, efficient defense — just 39% success allowed (vs ~44%); temper expectations for opposing skill players.

They lock down opposing WR2s — just 32 rec yds/game (vs ~36); fade receiving props there.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: opposing WR1/WR2 are the target — this D forces the throw.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
